subject: english-language
title: Transactional Writing Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the main transactional writing forms and what makes each tick.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language transactional writing walkthrough — letters, articles, speeches and leaflets.
final_note: You learned the key forms of transactional writing and the basics of register and audience.

concepts.def: Letter (Dear Sir/Madam), article (headline, byline), speech (direct address), report; conventions matter.
Inform, persuade, argue, explain, advise; word choice shifts; persuasive uses emotive language.
Adjust register: formal for parliament, informal for peers; vocabulary, examples, references.
Article opens with attention-grabbing headline (often pun); subheadings break up text.
Opens paragraph stating main idea; rest develops it; clear navigation for reader.
Acknowledge opposing view ('Some may argue...'); then refute; builds credibility in argument.

walkthroughs.body_html: A letter needs address and sign-off. An article needs a headline. Match the conventions.

Writing to your headteacher? Formal: full sentences, no contractions, 'Yours sincerely'.

Writing to a friend? Informal: contractions, slang, 'See ya'.
Teenagers want energy and humour. Local councillors want clarity and respect. Adjust vocabulary, examples and references to match.
